subject: spring-boot
summary: Explains Spring Boot project directory structure, dependency injection principles, and stereotype annotations for reading and navigating backend projects.
key_points: Spring Boot projects follow a layered structure: controller, service, repository, model.
Dependency injection lets the framework create and wire objects — reducing coupling.
Constructor injection is preferred over field injection for testability and clarity.
misconceptions: @Component and @Service have completely different runtime behavior.
Field injection with @Autowired is the standard approach.
Classes outside the base package are automatically scanned.
check_questions: What is dependency injection and why is it useful?
What is the difference between @Service and @Repository?
Why is constructor injection preferred over field injection?

fact_candidates: Role of each Spring stereotype annotation
Definition and purpose of dependency injection
practical_judgment_candidates: Choosing constructor injection vs field injection
Identifying which layer should contain business logic
scenario_candidates: Tracing request flow from Controller to Service to Repository
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Assuming all classes in the project are auto-scanned
